pull.title: validation: don't treat snapshot block as linked on startup
pull.body:
Background sync requests blocks up to and including the snapshot block from several peers at once, so the snapshot block can be stored before one of its ancestors. `ReceivedBlockTransactions()` then keeps it in `m_blocks_unlinked`, but that isn't persisted. On restart `LoadBlockIndex()` gives it the hardcoded `m_chain_tx_count`, `PopulateBlockIndexCandidates()` makes it a background candidate, and `FindMostWorkChain()` walks back to its parent, which has no chain tx count:

```
Assertion failed: (pindexTest->HaveNumChainTxs() || pindexTest->nHeight == 0), function FindMostWorkChain, file validation.cpp, line 3217.
```

It needs a restart in that window, so it should be rare, but after that the node aborts on every start. The only ways out I found are `-reindex-chainstate` or `-reindex`, and both delete the snapshot chainstate.

Fix this by adding the snapshot block to `m_blocks_unlinked` on startup if an ancestor is missing, and not making it a background candidate until then. Both are needed, without the first one background validation stalls. A node that is already stuck starts with the fix and finishes background validation without a reindex.

The new step in `feature_assumeutxo.py` restarts the node after the snapshot block is submitted out of order, and fails on master. I also reproduced it over p2p with a test peer that withholds the snapshot block's parent.

These are the two changes from #35307 (closed, the motivation there was `submitblock` before `loadtxoutset`) without its blockfile and VerifyDB changes. cyb3ralbert hit the same assertion while testing #36452 (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36452#issuecomment-6464524112), which is still needed when the snapshot tip is at the snapshot block. #36149 drops the `BLOCK_HAVE_DATA` check in the branch right below, so whichever is merged second should match it.

Ideally, start with the one that should be merged first.

Tested `feature_assumeutxo.py` at `80f6ddd` on Windows x64: passes with the fix. Reverting only the two C++ changes while keeping the new test reproduces the startup assertion in `FindMostWorkChain()`.

Can target_block->pprev be null under mock parameters in unit tests? pindex->pprev is dereferenced directly without a null guard before checking HaveNumChainTxs(), whereas the loop below explicitly guards against null parents.

Reverting the two C++ hunks against 80f6ddd6c reproduces the SIGABRT at validation.cpp:3217 in FindMostWorkChain. With the patch, feature_assumeutxo.py and validation unit tests pass locally.

PR #36149 drops BLOCK_HAVE_DATA in LoadBlockIndex so pruned blocks without data stay in m_blocks_unlinked while waiting for parents. Whichever lands second will need to align that branch.

> Can target_block->pprev be null under mock parameters in unit tests?

The target block is only set on the historical chainstate to the snapshot base block (in [`AddChainstate`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/80f6ddd6cbba7c8104dc0b9dabb451af13cc4a7d/src/validation.cpp#L6272)), which has to match an assumeutxo entry from chainparams and is never genesis. The unit tests create snapshot chainstates on non-genesis blocks as well (or clear the target immediately). The `pprev == nullptr` guard further down in the loop is for genesis when iterating all block indices.

Could you add `wait_for_full_init=False` to the [restart](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/80f6ddd6cbba7c8104dc0b9dabb451af13cc4a7d/test/functional/feature_assumeutxo.py#L680-L685) for current master?

The test waits for index sync before establishing the peer connection needed to complete it. With this change, `feature_assumeutxo.py` passes.

events.message:
validation: don't treat snapshot block as linked on startup

If the snapshot block is received during background sync before some
of its ancestors, ReceivedBlockTransactions() adds it to
m_blocks_unlinked and it isn't a background candidate until the
missing blocks arrive.

LoadBlockIndex() doesn't restore this on restart. The snapshot block
gets its m_chain_tx_count from the assumeutxo data and is never added
to m_blocks_unlinked, so PopulateBlockIndexCandidates() makes it a
background candidate. FindMostWorkChain() then walks back to its
parent, which has m_chain_tx_count 0, and hits the HaveNumChainTxs()
assert. This happens on every restart.

Add the block to m_blocks_unlinked on startup if an ancestor is
missing, and skip it as a background candidate until then. Without
the m_blocks_unlinked entry the block isn't picked up when the
missing blocks arrive, and background validation stalls.

Extend feature_assumeutxo.py to restart the node in this state.

events.body:
> Could you add `wait_for_full_init=False` to the restart for current master?

Rebased and done.
